newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian army closes ranks around jailed general.
newsitem.headline: Colombian army closes ranks around jailed general.

text.p: Colombia's Army commander Gen. Harold Bedoya heaped praise on Saturday on a retired three-star general who stands accused of organising right-wing paramilitary groups that killed hundreds of leftists and suspected rebel sympathisers in the 1980s.
"General Yanine is one of Colombia's illustrious generals," Bedoya told reporters.

Gen. Farouk Yanine Diaz, an adviser to the Washington-based Interamerican Defence College, returned to Colombia earlier this month for questioning about his alleged links to the paramilitary groups that killed with impunity throughout the so-called Magdalena Medio region of northern Colombia in the mid-1980s as part of a "dirty war" against leftist guerrillas.
Formal "conspiracy" charges were filed against Yanine on Friday and he was ordered jailed without benefit of bail, judicial sources said.
"He (Yanine) is the general who did the most for Colombia in his time," Bedoya said of the highest-ranking Colombian general to be accused of human rights violations.
"Thanks to General Yanine, the Magdalena Medio has been pacified," he added. "I only wish that Colombia had a lot of generals with General Yanine's qualities."

Alonso de Jesus Baquero, a self-confessed paramilitary chieftain jailed in southwest Valle province, has testfied that he carried out more than 800 political murders in the Magdalena Medio region in the mid-1980s.
He has accused Yanine of orchestrating paramilitary activity in the area and tacitly approving the torture-murder of 19 merchants there in 1987.

The merchants were suspected of sympathising with rebel groups operating in the region at the time, according to published accounts of testimony by Baquero, a former guerrilla known by his alias as "Vladimir."

Colombia has one of the worst human rights records in the Americas. Leading watchdog groups like Amnesty International have consistently pointed to the military, and criticised the impunity with which crimes are committed within its ranks.
